learning_objectives.en: Track speakers’ agreed decisions, not just initial suggestions.
learning_objectives.vi: Theo dõi quyết định đã thống nhất, không chọn đề xuất ban đầu.

content.en: In a two-speaker discussion, an initial idea may be rejected. Listening answers often depend on the final agreement.
content.vi: Trong hội thoại hai người, một ý kiến ban đầu có thể bị từ chối. Đáp án thường dựa vào quyết định cuối.

strategies.en: Note “suggested”, “problem”, “agreed”. Listen for “but”, “instead”, “you’re right”, and corrections.
strategies.vi: Ghi “đề xuất”, “vấn đề”, “chốt”. Nghe các dấu hiệu but, instead, you’re right và sửa ý.

mini_review.en: Can you name two suggestions that were changed before agreement?
mini_review.vi: Bạn nêu được hai đề xuất ban đầu sau đó bị thay đổi?

audios.title: Planning a survey on student leisure
audios.transcript:
Kim: So, Sam, we need to decide how to run our survey on how students spend their free time.
Sam: Right. I thought we could just put a questionnaire online and share the link with everyone in our year.
Kim: That would be quick, but I’m worried that only the most organised students would answer. Tutor Ellis said online surveys often get a very low response rate.
Sam: Fair point. What if we hand out paper questionnaires at the start of lectures instead?
Kim: Yes, that should give us more answers, and from a wider range of students. Let’s do that.
Sam: OK. How many questions should we include? I wrote twenty-five.
Kim: That’s too many for a lecture break. People will stop halfway. I’d say twelve at most.
Sam: Twelve, then. I’ll remove the ones about music, because they overlap with the questions on social media.
Kim: Good idea. Now, what do you think will be the most interesting result?
Sam: Honestly, I expect sport to be less popular than people think. Most students I know say they’re too busy.
Kim: I think the result about part-time work will be more interesting. If many students work twenty hours a week, that explains a lot about their free time.
Sam: True. We should definitely ask about working hours.
Kim: What about the presentation? Ellis wants it in two weeks.
Sam: I’d like to show the results as pie charts.
Kim: Pie charts are fine for one question, but we want to compare first-year and final-year students, so bar charts would work better.
Sam: You’re right. Bar charts it is.
Kim: And one last thing – we should explain the limitations of our survey at the end. Only students on our course will answer, so we can’t say the results apply to the whole university.
Sam: Agreed. I’ll write that section, and you can do the introduction.
